mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% median) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST QoQ change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1% median) during episodes meeting the dual GDPC1/HOUST trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately driving higher inflation expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% median) when UNRATE < 3.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5% median) during four-month INDPRO declines below -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise of more than 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall of more than 2% in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) within a single month signals a sharp deterioration in labor market conditions, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE change > 0.4pp AND PAYEMS change < -2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1% median) during months meeting the UNRATE/PAYEMS trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPIAUCSL) below 1.5% for six consecutive months signals a persistent disinflationary environment, which lowers long-term real interest rates and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change < 1.5% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.5% median) during six-month periods of CPIAUCSL < 1.5% monthly change.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month signals a deepening recession, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% AND PAYEMS change < -1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1% median) during months meeting the UNRATE/PAYEMS recession trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase of more than 0.3% in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for eight consecutive months signals robust consumer demand expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days under any monetary regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.5% median) during eight-month periods of GDPC1 monthly increases above 0.3%.
